events.title: Pittsburgh Is Founded
events.description: After British forces captured Fort Duquesne from the French during the French and Indian War, the site at the meeting of the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers was renamed Pittsburgh.
events.significance: The strategic fork of the Ohio River became one of America's great industrial cities, and its capture helped tip the balance of power in North America toward Britain.

events.title: The British Leave New York City
events.description: Three months after the Treaty of Paris was signed, the last British troops left New York City. Residents celebrated the day for generations as Evacuation Day.
events.significance: The departure ended the British military presence in the new United States and symbolized the real end of the American Revolutionary War.

events.title: Poland's Last King Abdicates
events.description: Stanislaus August Poniatowski, the last king of the independent Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, was forced to abdicate and went into exile in Russia.
events.significance: His abdication followed the partitions of Poland. Poland then disappeared as an independent state for more than a century, until 1918.

events.title: HMS Barham Sinks
events.description: The British battleship HMS Barham was hit by a German torpedo during World War II and sank in the Mediterranean.
events.significance: The loss was one of the Royal Navy's heaviest of the war, and it showed how dangerous U-boats were to Allied naval power.

events.title: UN Creates a Day Against Violence Toward Women
events.description: The United Nations established November 25 as the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women.
events.significance: The date now anchors yearly global campaigns, including 16 Days of Activism, that raise awareness and push for action on gender-based violence.
